title: Construction of the canonical formal glueing functor
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring map, $t\in\mathbf N$, and $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$. In the category of formal glueing data [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] there exists a functor $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ with $\mathrm{Can}(M)=(S\otimes_R M,(M_{f_i})_i,(c^M_{f_i})_i,(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j})_{i,j})$ on every object and $\mathrm{Can}(h)=(1\otimes h,(h_{f_i})_i)$ on every linear map. The object components are equal as bundled modules, and structural maps and morphism components are the actual canonical maps, identified by heterogeneous equality after these equalities. No flatness or quotient hypothesis is assumed. Base change and localizations have the meanings in [def-weil-module-base-change] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away].

proof.text: (Part (1): $c$, $\sigma$ and the object $\mathrm{Can}(M)$.) For every $R$-module $P$ and $f,g\in R$, $\sigma^P_{f,g}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\sigma^P_{g,f}$, given by $(p/f^a)/g^b\mapsto(p/g^b)/f^a$, and $c^P_f$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism given by $(p\otimes s)/f^e\mapsto(p/f^e)\otimes s$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (2), (3). Let $M$ be an $R$-module. $M\otimes_RS$ is an $S$-module [def-weil-module-base-change] and $M_{f_i}$ an $R_{f_i}$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], so $\mathrm{Can}(M)=(M\otimes_RS,(M_{f_i}),(c^M_{f_i}),(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}))$ has the data required in [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. Condition (a) for it reads $(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}\otimes_RS)\circ c^{M_{f_i}}_{f_j}\circ(c^M_{f_i})_{f_j}=c^{M_{f_j}}_{f_i}\circ(c^M_{f_j})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M\otimes S}_{f_i,f_j}$. By the formulas just quoted and the formula $h_f(x/f^e)=h(x)/f^e$ for the localization of a map [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], both sides send $((m\otimes s)/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ to $((m/f_j^b)/f_i^a)\otimes s$: the left side via $((m/f_i^a)\otimes s)/f_j^b$ and $((m/f_i^a)/f_j^b)\otimes s$, the right side via $((m\otimes s)/f_j^b)/f_i^a$ and $((m/f_j^b)\otimes s)/f_i^a$. Every element of $((M\otimes_RS)_{f_i})_{f_j}$ is a finite sum of such elements ($x/f^e$ with $x$ a sum of pure tensors, and $(\sum x_k)/f^e=\sum x_k/f^e$), and both sides are additive, so (a) holds. Condition (b) reads $(\sigma^M_{f_j,f_k})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M_{f_j}}_{f_i,f_k}\circ(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j})_{f_k}=\sigma^{M_{f_k}}_{f_i,f_j}\circ(\sigma^M_{f_i,f_k})_{f_j}\circ\sigma^{M_{f_i}}_{f_j,f_k}$; every element of $((M_{f_i})_{f_j})_{f_k}$ is $((m/f_i^a)/f_j^b)/f_k^c$, and both sides send it to $((m/f_k^c)/f_j^b)/f_i^a$ (left: via $((m/f_j^b)/f_i^a)/f_k^c$, $((m/f_j^b)/f_k^c)/f_i^a$; right: via $((m/f_i^a)/f_k^c)/f_j^b$, $((m/f_k^c)/f_i^a)/f_j^b$). So $\mathrm{Can}(M)$ is an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$.

proof.text: (Part (1): $\mathrm{Can}$ on maps; functoriality.) Let $u:M\to N$ be $R$-linear. Then $u\otimes_RS$ is $S$-linear [def-weil-module-base-change] and $u_{f_i}$ is $R$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The two conditions for $\mathrm{Can}(u)=(u\otimes_RS,(u_{f_i}))$ to be a morphism [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] are $c^N_{f_i}\circ(u\otimes_RS)_{f_i}=(u_{f_i}\otimes_RS)\circ c^M_{f_i}$ and $\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\circ(u_{f_i})_{f_j}=(u_{f_j})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}$. By the formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] both sides of the first send $(m\otimes s)/f_i^e$ to $(u(m)/f_i^e)\otimes s$, and both sides of the second send $(m/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ to $(u(m)/f_j^b)/f_i^a$; these elements generate the sources additively (step 1), so both hold. Since $(v\circ u)\otimes_RS=(v\otimes_RS)\circ(u\otimes_RS)$, $\mathrm{id}\otimes_RS=\mathrm{id}$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $(v\circ u)_f=v_f\circ u_f$ and $(\mathrm{id})_f=\mathrm{id}$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (1), and composition and identities in $\mathrm{Glue}$ are componentwise [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], $\mathrm{Can}$ is a functor $\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}$. This proves (1). For later use: for an $R$-linear $u$, $\mathrm{Can}(u)$ being a morphism is the naturality $c^N_{f}\circ(u\otimes_RS)_{f}=(u_{f}\otimes_RS)\circ c^M_{f}$, $\sigma^N_{f,g}\circ(u_{f})_{g}=(u_{g})_{f}\circ\sigma^M_{f,g}$.

theorem exists_canonical_functor {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R) :
    ∃ Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f,
      (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))) ∧
      (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (h : M ⟶ N),
        HEq (Can.map h).prime (extendMap φ h.hom) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.map h).chart i) (localMap (f i) h.hom))
